title: North Korea Fires Back-to-Back Ballistic Missiles as Tensions Spike Over US Military Drills
snippet: Pyongyang launched two short-range ballistic missiles within hours of each other on Sunday, marking its second major weapons test in a week following sharp warnings directed at Washington and its regional allies.
content:
SEOUL — North Korea launched a pair of short-range ballistic missiles off its eastern coast on Sunday, conducting rapid back-to-back tests just hours apart in a provocative display of military force aimed at the United States and its regional allies.

According to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff, the first weapon lifted off around 3:00 p.m. local time from the coastal Wonsan area, traveling roughly 280 miles (450 km). Military officials suspect the projectile belongs to Pyongyang's Hwasong-11 missile series.

Rapid Succession Offensives

Barely three hours later, at approximately 5:50 p.m., North Korea launched a second short-range missile from the same location. That projectile flew more than 370 miles (600 km) before landing in the waters outside Japan's exclusive economic zone, Japanese officials confirmed.

The dual tests represent Pyongyang's second major weapons demonstration in roughly a week, following an initial launch on September 12. The rapid-fire maneuvers come shortly after North Korea publicly rejected a UN nuclear watchdog resolution and lashed out at joint US-led naval drills conducted near Guam late last month alongside South Korea and Japan.

Condemnation from Washington, Seoul, and Tokyo

Military intelligence agencies from the U.S., South Korea, and Japan closely tracked the developments in real time, sharing radar and trajectory data. South Korea's National Security Council quickly issued a stern rebuke, emphasizing that Pyongyang's repeated missile tests violate long-standing UN Security Council resolutions.

Tokyo also took immediate action, lodging a formal diplomatic protest through embassy channels in Beijing. Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi warned that North Korea's escalating aggression directly threatens peace and security across the Indo-Pacific region.

The Sunday launches follow fiery rhetoric from Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. On Friday, she accused the U.S. and its allies of driving peninsula tensions to dangerous new highs, vowing that North Korea will accelerate the build-up of its nuclear arsenal despite international pressure.
